newsitem.title: FRANCE: Metaleurop details dollar, metals impact.
newsitem.headline: Metaleurop details dollar, metals impact.

text.p: Non-ferrous metals producer Metaleurop said on Wednesday that a fluctuation of 10 centimes in the dollar/franc parity had an impact of 28 million francs on its earnings.
In a document distributed during a press briefing Metaleurop also said a fluctuation of $10 per tonne in the price of lead or zinc had an impact of five million francs on earnings.
Metaleurop expects earnings to improve in year 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) on the back of higher metal prices and cost savings linked to restructuring.
But board member Christian Bue said that because the group's financial year starts in October, Metaleurop did not benefit during its first quarter from a better metal and dollar environment.

"Zinc prices have been rising for six weeks and the dollar started firming in early January but our fiscal year starts on October 1. So we have a full quarter that will not benefit (from these conditions)," he said.
Bue also explained that Metaleurop tries to spread most supply contracts over three financial years, which limits the impact of currency and metal prices fluctuations on a given year.
Metaleurop reported a 1995/96 net profit of 42 million francs compared with a loss of 122 million francs the previous year. Metaleurop is a unit of German group Preussag.
